I’d like to share an experience that left me deeply disappointed. I’ve been getting orthodontic treatment at another clinic, and on this particular day, a wire from my braces pierced into my mouth, causing a severe wound. I had to endure the pain while working all day, and by the time I got off work, I intended to visit my regular clinic—but it was pouring rain nonstop, and I couldn’t make it there in time.

To make matters worse, I had an international flight that night at midnight. I urgently needed to find the nearest dental clinic to simply clip the wire that was cutting into my mouth. It was a quick and simple procedure—many clinics would help out in such situations, even for walk-ins, and some would charge a fee, which is totally acceptable.

However, when I arrived at this clinic around 7:00 PM, drenched from the rain and clearly in pain, hoping for just basic assistance before my long flight—I was outright rejected. The reason? “I wasn't a previous customer.” There was no effort to listen or I'd like to share an unpleasant experience.

While I understand each clinic has its own policies, I strongly believe that as a healthcare provider, the priority should be the well-being of people in need—regardless of whether they've been here before. The complete lack of compassion and refusal to help in such a straightforward case was disheartening.

I hope this review serves as a reflection point for the clinic to reconsider how it approaches emergency walk-ins and basic human decency in the future.

I'm sharing a negative experience. I was getting braces at a clinic, and one day a wire poked my mouth, causing a gaping wound. I had to work all day in great pain. After work, I intended to rush to my regular clinic, but it was raining heavily, making it impossible to get there on time.

Even worse, I had an international flight at midnight that night, so I needed to quickly find the nearest clinic to have the wire removed. It's a minor procedure, not difficult, and many places were kind enough to help, even if I wasn't a regular patient. Some even charged a fee, which I was happy to accept.

Upon arriving at the clinic around 7:00 PM, I was almost completely soaked from the rain. I hoped to receive some basic medical assistance before my long journey, but I was refused simply because I had "never been a customer before," and there was no indication that any help would be provided.

While I understand that each clinic has its own policies, as a medical facility whose primary duty is to care for patients, whether new or returning, I believe such a heartless refusal is unacceptable.

I hope this review serves as a reflection for future improvements to your service.
